messages:
rachel: quick note — ran onboarding sweep for psi-embed-v1 with int4-perchannel on staging. short-query recall@5 down ~7% vs psi-embed-v0.8. anyone free to eyeball? :thinking:
Noah: lemme see the command and a few numbers please
rachel: `./evals/recall_k.sh --model psi-embed-v1 --quant int4 --bench short-queries --k 5 --index k10-prod`
rachel: top-line: baseline (v0.8 fp16) recall@5 = 0.915
rachel: psi-embed-v1 int4-perchannel recall@5 = 0.846
rachel: delta = -0.069 (~7.5% relative)
Diego: ouch. is this across all cohorts or a specific tail? can you break down by query length and lang?\rnachel: (typo) uploading breakdown csv to s3: s3://redwood-evals/psi/v1/shortq/breakdown.csv
Noah: ran quick L2 histogram compare, mean norms: v0.8=4.18, v1-int4=3.97. that's a notable shift for short queries.
Diego: run paired idflip on top 2k samples: `python tools/idflip.py --old psi-v0.8 --new psi-v1 --sample 2000 --k 5`
eval-bot: idflip queued (job psi-17483). ETA ~2m
Noah: also check whitening / mean-centering step — we changed whitening lambda during v1 training. small miscalib + quant could amplify.
Diego: running umap for 400 anchors now: `scripts/vis/umap.py --model psi-embed-v1 --quant int4 --anchors 400 --out psi_v1_int4_umap.png`
rachel: uploaded umap: https://console.redwood/embeds/psi/1748309000/umap.png — looks like a couple clusters collapsed at the edges.
Noah: infra-bot: deploy psi-v1-int4 staging succeeded. p50 latency +3ms, memory -18% compared to v0.8
Diego: try int6-perchannel and int4-pertensor to isolate whether per-channel scaling or bitwidth is culprit. also run symmetric vs asymmetric quant calibrations.
Noah: kicked int6-perchannel run.
eval-bot: int6 run complete. recall@5 = 0.908 (close to baseline)
rachel: that narrows it to int4 quantization.
Diego: hypothesis: per-channel int4 scaling with asymmetric zero-point introduces bias for short queries. propose we test symmetric clipping and per-tensor int4 as a quick probe.
Noah: i'll spin per-tensor int4 and symmetric int4 calibrations now. also starting a focused bisect on the quantizer code — recent change to rounding mode two commits ago. ticket Q-812 in progress.
Noah: per-tensor int4 recall@5 = 0.900 (better but still slightly below baseline)
rachel: symmetric int4 recall@5 = 0.912 (almost baseline!) interesting.
Diego: that suggests asymmetric per-channel q + int4 is the main issue. likely zero-point skew. can you dump scale/zero arrays for a few layers?
Noah: scale/zero for layer3 conv-like block: scales differ 2-3x across channels on short-query embeddings. attaching s3://redwood-evals/psi/v1/scales/layer3.csv
Diego: small fix candidate: use symmetric quant for int4 or enforce per-channel clipping at 3 sigma before scale calc. i'll prototype a patch and run quick eval.
Noah: ops: suggestion to hold int4 rollout and prefer int6-perchannel for production until we harden int4. ops, any objections?
ops: agree. prefer safe step — route traffic to int6 until we confirm symmetric int4 stable across cohorts. will update routing policy after we get Diego's patch results.
rachel: thanks team. action items: Diego prototype symmetric/per-channel clip patch + quick eval, Noah finish bisect and attach failing commit if any, ops hold int4 rollout. we'll sync in 45m if needed. :thumbsup:
